experiment: Controlled Intervention 3 - Investigator requester-resolvability classification for conflicts
change: Investigator _ASSESS_SYSTEM prompt: when readings genuinely conflict, classify gap_user_resolvable (true=requester can supply/repeat/confirm a discriminator; false=needs technician/expert/inspection/unavailable instrument) and never leave it null for a genuine unresolved conflict.

primary_mechanism.arc07_assess_own_conflict: False 5/5 - established from the diagnostic LOGS (the RETRIEVAL line's assess conflict), NOT from the run artifacts, which persist only the final merged evidence_conflict=True. The assess model does not register the SAT readings as a genuine conflict (it reconciles them as a sensor fault), so the resolvability instruction (gated on a perceived conflict) never engages and gap stays None.

contrast_arc08.result: correct and preserved (was already correct pre-intervention)

false_resolvability_or_spurious_ask.note: 1 of 5 runs only; ARC-16 is normally a skip case, so this required a triage variance into the retrieval branch; a minor, non-recurring blip, not a broad/material regression

unrelated_variance_note: decision 16->15.8, grounding 6->5.4, structured 19.2->18.6 do NOT pass through the changed conflict-gap classification (ARC-07/ARC-08 decisions are unchanged). The artifacts alone do not establish the specific cause, so this movement is reported as unrelated run-to-run model variance and is NOT attributed to this intervention. Latency 10.2->12.2s reported as observed only.
verdict: FALSIFIED (stands on the artifact mechanism_state fields alone): ARC-07 gap=None 5/5, ESCALATE(conflict_unresolvable) 5/5, ASK 0/5. Root cause, from the diagnostic logs (the artifacts persist only the final merged conflict): the assess step's own evidence_conflict is False 5/5, so a prompt instruction gated on a perceived conflict cannot engage for ARC-07 - the conflict exists only at the state level via Intervention 2's triage-OR merge, which the assess prompt never sees. ARC-08 stayed correctly unresolvable (already correct pre-intervention, so not evidence the intervention works). One minor spurious ASK (ARC-16, 1/5) - not materially harmful.
structural_finding: Driving gap classification for a PRESERVED conflict purely from the assess prompt cannot work when the assess model itself does not register the conflict. A real fix would pass the triage-detected conflict into the assess step (so it classifies resolvability for the conflict that was actually detected) - a combined code+prompt change, a future candidate, NOT attempted here.
remaining_untouched_clusters: ARC-07 gap-classification (still open; needs triage-conflict passed into assess)
note_artifact_baseline_field: internal 'baseline' field is a hardcoded harness constant; experiment identity = path + git_commit 214924e.

codex_post_review.resolution: corrected two interpretation overstatements: the assess-own-conflict root cause is log-derived (not artifact-visible), and the decision/grounding movement is reported as unrelated variance rather than asserted as a specific cause. Outcome counts unchanged.
